sessionTitle: Scale cloud-native workloads with Azure Linux

announcements.name: Azure Container Linux is generally available
announcements.shortDescription: Microsoft's hardened, immutable Azure Linux image for AKS reached GA at Build, derived from the Flatcar Container Linux distribution.
announcements.longDescription: Azure Container Linux became generally available the day of the talk, presented as an immutable distribution for AKS that delivers additional support and consistency. It is positioned as part of the 'one OS everywhere' story, letting the same application run across WSL, Azure Linux VMs, and AKS with the same experience. The speakers highlight immutability as a key selling point and promise a dedicated demo for it.

announcements.name: Azure Linux 4.0 VM image enters public preview
announcements.shortDescription: The VM image is now available to test, validate, and provide feedback on.
announcements.longDescription: The Azure Linux 4.0 VM image is now in public preview and available for users to use, test, validate, and provide feedback on. It is part of the consistent 'same OS everywhere' experience spanning WSL, VMs, containers, and Azure Container Linux, using the same Python version, kernel, and internal libraries so an application validated on one runs across all. The presenters note they will share later how to reach out with feedback.

announcements.name: Azure Linux 4.0 on WSL
announcements.shortDescription: Demonstrated running live, with WSL preview noted as a fast follow.
announcements.longDescription: Porvi [inferred] demonstrated Azure Linux 4.0 running live through WSL, verifying on stage that the WSL instance was actually running on Azure Linux 4.0. A simple Python application was started in WSL to later be shown running identically on an Azure Linux VM and on AKS, illustrating the 'one OS everywhere' consistency. The demo emphasized running Azure Linux across WSL, VMs, and Kubernetes with declarative deviations that reduce surface area and CVEs.

announcements.name: Kernel 6.18 maintained for the distribution lifetime
announcements.shortDescription: Azure Linux 4.0 ships the latest upstream kernel, to be maintained across the distribution's life.
announcements.longDescription: After SSHing into an Azure Linux 4.0 VM, the presenter showed it running kernel 6.18 [inferred] (transcribed as '618'), described as the latest upstream kernel that will be maintained for the lifetime of the distribution. The segment also highlighted security, with SELinux [inferred] enabled by default in enforcing mode out-of-the-box, and 'declarative deviations' that keep the image lean and optimized for Azure and cloud-native workloads.
